cards.front: How do you reverse a string in Java?
cards.back: No reverse method on String — use new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString()
cards.extra: String is immutable, so reversing means building a new one. A manual loop works, but the builder is the idiomatic answer.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: How do you check whether a string is a palindrome?
cards.back: Compare characters from both ends inward until they meet or mismatch
cards.extra: Case and whitespace usually need normalising first; comparing against the reversed string is shorter but allocates.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: What is the efficient way to test primality?
cards.back: Loop divisors from 2 up to √n — past that, any factor would have a matching one below
cards.extra: Checking to n-1 is correct but wasteful. 2 is the smallest prime, and values below 2 are not prime.

cards.front: How do you generate Fibonacci numbers iteratively?
cards.back: Track the previous two values and add them in a loop — O(n) time, O(1) space
cards.extra: The recursive version is exponential because it recomputes the same values; that is the point of the exercise.

cards.front: How do you swap two variables?
cards.back: With a temporary variable: temp = a; a = b; b = temp;
cards.extra: Arithmetic or XOR tricks avoid the temp but break on overflow and are unreadable. Java has no tuple swap.

cards.front: How do you sort an array of numbers?
cards.back: Arrays.sort(a) — ascending order, in place
cards.extra: Descending order needs a boxed array, because the comparator overload does not accept primitives.

cards.front: How do you turn a string into a character array?
cards.back: str.toCharArray(); for words use split(" ")
cards.extra: toCharArray gives chars; split gives String[] and takes a regex, so a literal dot must be escaped.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: How do you remove duplicates from an array?
cards.back: Copy into a LinkedHashSet (preserves order), then back to an array
cards.extra: A HashSet is faster but unordered; sorting first then skipping neighbours works with no extra memory.

cards.front: How do you find the second largest element?
cards.back: One pass tracking the largest and the second largest separately
cards.extra: Sorting and taking length-2 is simpler but O(n log n), and wrong when the maximum value repeats.

cards.front: How do you count character frequencies?
cards.back: A Map<Character,Integer> updated with merge(ch, 1, Integer::sum)
cards.extra: merge removes the get-or-default pattern: one call replaces containsKey, get and put.

cards.front: How do you check whether two strings are anagrams?
cards.back: Sort both char arrays and compare, or count characters into a 26-slot array
cards.extra: Sorting is O(n log n) and short; counting is O(n) but assumes a known alphabet.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: How do you find the GCD of two numbers?
cards.back: Euclid's algorithm: while (b != 0) { int t = b; b = a % b; a = t; }
cards.extra: Each remainder pair shrinks fast, so it converges in O(log n) instead of testing every divisor.

cards.front: How do you sum the digits of a number?
cards.back: Repeatedly add n % 10 and divide n by 10 until it reaches 0
cards.extra: For a String of digits, subtract '0' from each char instead.

cards.front: How do you reverse the digits of a number?
cards.back: Accumulate rev = rev * 10 + n % 10, dividing n by 10 each round
cards.extra: Textbook integer reversal — it overflows for large inputs unless you accumulate in a long.

cards.front: How do you generate a random integer in a range?
cards.back: (int)(Math.random() * (max - min + 1)) + min
cards.extra: Math.random returns [0,1): multiply by the width, cast, then shift by min. Random.nextInt(bound) is cleaner.

cards.front: How do you shuffle an array?
cards.back: Wrap it with Arrays.asList and call Collections.shuffle(list)
cards.extra: That view is fixed-size but writable, which is exactly what shuffle needs; a manual Fisher-Yates loop avoids the wrapper.

cards.front: How do you merge two arrays?
cards.back: System.arraycopy(src, srcPos, dest, destPos, length) twice into a preallocated array
cards.extra: It is a native bulk copy — much faster than a loop, and it copies references rather than deep-cloning.

cards.front: How do you iterate a HashMap?
cards.back: for (Map.Entry<K,V> e : map.entrySet())
cards.extra: entrySet avoids a second lookup per entry; keySet plus get does the work twice.

cards.front: How do you loop over enum constants?
cards.back: for (Type t : Type.values())
cards.extra: values() returns a fresh copy on each call, so cache it in a static field in hot code.

cards.front: What are the two groups of Java modifiers?
cards.back: Access (public, private, protected, default) and non-access (static, final, abstract, synchronized, volatile, transient, native, strictfp)
cards.extra: Access modifiers decide visibility; non-access ones change behaviour and memory semantics.

cards.front: What does transient do to a field?
cards.back: Excludes it from serialization; on deserialization it comes back as its default value
cards.extra: Usually paired with a custom writeObject that persists the data in another form.

cards.front: Name the four core collection interfaces and their shapes.
cards.back: List (ordered, duplicates), Set (unique), Queue (FIFO), Map (key→value)
cards.extra: Map is not a Collection — it has no iterator over elements, only over entries.

cards.front: What is var, and what is it not?
cards.back: Local-variable type inference (Java 10) — the type is still fixed at compile time
cards.extra: It cannot be used for fields, parameters or return types, and it needs an initialiser.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::07 Variables and Scopes

cards.front: Why wrap a FileWriter in a BufferedWriter?
cards.back: To batch writes and get newLine(), which writes the platform line separator
cards.extra: newLine() is the portable alternative to writing \n by hand.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: Which class creates and writes files in modern Java?
cards.back: java.nio.file.Files — createFile, writeString, delete
cards.extra: The older File.createNewFile() still works but throws less descriptive errors.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::02 File Operations

cards.front: What separates an inner class from a static nested class?
cards.back: An inner class holds a hidden reference to the outer instance; a static nested class does not
cards.extra: That reference lets it touch outer fields, and is why inner objects leak the outer one.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::05 Nested Classes

cards.front: What does TreeMap give you that HashMap does not?
cards.back: Entries sorted by key, with O(log n) operations instead of O(1)
cards.extra: Keys must be Comparable or you supply a Comparator; null keys are rejected.
